deep.reconstruction:
The page holds sketches for representing arrangements ('systems') of pseudo-lines in the real projective plane by sweeps and wiring diagrams. It is drawn on the back of a CRAY2 line-printer banner listing dated 19 Aug 82.

(1) Top left: a rectangle with ticks A B C D E F G H along the top edge (arrow pointing right) and H G F E D C B A along the bottom edge. A downward arrow marks the sweep direction. This is the standard picture of the projective plane, or of a Möbius band, cut open along a line at infinity. Each pseudo-line enters at the top and leaves at the bottom, and the boundary identification reverses the order. So a simple arrangement of n pseudo-lines becomes a strip diagram whose output permutation is the full reversal of the input. A few roughly horizontal lines (sweep positions) are drawn across it.

(2) Top right: a wiring diagram of 7 strands A to G. Horizontal sweep levels are numbered 1 to 11 on the right; the intervals between them are numbered 1' to 9' on the left. Crossings are dotted and occur at successive levels. D and E cross first, then F and G, then a cascade follows. One strand (G) runs diagonally from top right to bottom left, crossing every other strand in turn. There is heavy reworking in the centre, apparently testing alternative positions of a triangle of crossings. The strand order is recorded along the bottom of the diagram as G A E D C F B. This is not the full reversal, so the figure shows a partial sweep: a path of adjacent transpositions in the weak Bruhat order of S_7, i.e. a piece of an allowable sequence. Equivalently it shows how inserting one new pseudo-line threads through an existing wiring.

(3) Bottom right: the same 7-strand grid on squared lines 1 to 11. Only one strand is followed diagonally: a pseudo-line sweeping across the others. A and G are thickened at the bottom, and the final labels read G A. This looks like the isolated history of one inserted line and its crossings.

(4) Centre: a 'tree' of dashed arrows. Strands D, E, F, G merge pairwise at two dots, then into one point, then fan back out into branches ending in X-shaped crossings. This suggests schematically how local crossing events compose or are organised, perhaps as a cell or poset structure on crossing events.

(5) Left middle: a lens-shaped band with zigzag strands touching its two boundary curves. This reads as a strip neighbourhood of a pseudo-line, with other pseudo-lines crossing it, drawn as triangles.

(6) Bottom left: two horizontal lines with two crossing lines meeting at one point. One line is drawn twice, slightly displaced. This illustrates a triple point being perturbed, i.e. a triangle flip (Ringel move, Reidemeister-III-type mutation) between simple arrangements.

(7) Bottom centre: a cylinder. The top rim carries labels G F E D; the bottom rim carries A B C, then D E F, then C B A G. This is the annulus double cover of the Möbius band (the sphere-minus-poles picture of RP^2). Each pseudo-line lifts to a closed curve meeting both rims at antipodal points, with labels repeating in reversed order around the circle.

Overall purpose: to set up combinatorial encodings (sweeps, wiring diagrams, allowable sequences, the cylinder/double-cover model) for classifying pseudo-line arrangements and their mutations.
errors: The output order G A E D C F B under the big diagram is not the full reversal G F E D C B A. Either the diagram depicts only a partial sweep (levels 1-11 do not exhaust the crossings), or the labels record something else; on its own the figure is not a complete simple arrangement.
Heavy overwriting in the central part of the big diagram makes several crossings ambiguous; the exact transposition sequence cannot be read reliably.

ideas.what: Cutting RP^2 (Möbius band) along a line at infinity so that pseudo-lines become strands from top to bottom with order reversed
ideas.modern_name: wiring diagram / sweep representation of pseudoline arrangements

ideas.what: Sequence of adjacent transpositions recording successive crossings during a sweep
ideas.modern_name: allowable sequence of permutations / reduced words in S_n, paths in weak Bruhat order

ideas.what: Perturbation of a triple point into a small triangle
ideas.modern_name: triangle flip / Ringel mutation (Reidemeister III move)

ideas.what: Cylinder (annulus) as double cover of the Möbius band with antipodal labelling of line ends
ideas.modern_name: double cover S^2 -> RP^2 / great pseudocircle arrangements, oriented matroid rank 3 picture

ideas.what: Threading one new pseudo-line diagonally through an existing wiring
ideas.modern_name: single-element extension of a pseudoline arrangement (oriented matroid extension)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Levi (1926) extension lemma; Las Vergnas, Bokowski et al.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard combinatorial pictures of pseudoline arrangements: wiring diagrams, sweeps, triangle flips, the double cover. All are well established in the Goodman-Pollack / Ringel / oriented-matroid literature by 1983, and the page gives no new statement or result. Its main interest is biographical: it shows Grothendieck independently working out these encodings, and the paper is a reused CRAY2 printout.
transcription_corrections: Bottom labels of the top-left rectangle read 'H G F E D C B A' (the B is written like a D).

The printed background is an upside-down CRAY2 job banner: '****A END JOB 25 CRAY2 ROOM 9.03.23 AM 19 AUG 82 R6.PR1 SYS JES2 JOB 25 END A****'. The large letters C-R-A-Y and 'SS', and the 0/O block banner ('0025'), belong to this printout, not to Grothendieck's notes.
In the big diagram, 1'-9' label the intervals on the left and 1-11 the levels on the right; the strand order G A E D C F B is written along the bottom.
The cylinder labels are: top rim G F E (D at right); middle ring A B C; inner/back ring D E F; front bottom rim C B A G.
The page number '142' is written at the bottom left.
